translation_notes: The five `obsgraph.add` become three `+{ }` in the method (one run on `{self.sensor_id}` with `;`, one island per loop body), on `@graph obsgraph` declared once at module level after `obsgraph = cfg.get_graph()` and seen by the method. `cfg.sosa.Sensor`, `.observes`, `.implements` are `sosa:Sensor`, `sosa:observes`, `sosa:implements` through `from context_shim import sosa:` (the Namespace the module exports as `cfg.sosa`); `RDF`, `RDFS` from rdflib are imported as prefixes (`rdf:`, `rdfs:`).

The terms `self.sensor_id` (a BNode), `self.comment`, `self.label`, `obs.label` are bound objects and stay interpolations; `_:{ }` does not apply, the BNode is created by `BNode()` and kept on `self`.

Hollow-green trap avoided in the driver: the region writes to a MODULE graph, not to an argument, so each call's stub `self` carries that same graph (`self.graph`), which makes the harness canonicalise it after the call. Mutations checked: removing the `isinstance(pro, Procedure)` test and dropping `rdfs:comment` both FAIL.
Context shim: PySOSA is not installed. context_shim.py has `config` (the shared graph returned by get_graph(), the SOSA namespace) and ObservableProperty / Procedure reduced to their `label`.

Credit correction (2026-11-02, corpus/403 defect 3): dropped `rdf:` from the prefix import, declared by the mechanical draft but never used as a term in the translated region (and not among the bindings the original sets on its graph); `rdfeval check` stays OK.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: nearly nothing to compress -- only the redundant parentheses of `(args[3])`. The five obsgraph.add cannot be grouped by `obsgraph += [...]` without a `global obsgraph` (obsgraph is a module graph), which a reviewer would reject; the two filtered loops are already minimal; the order of the attribute assignments and of the adds is kept because the driver checks the IndexError and TypeError cases.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: same as translated.ldpy (one +{ } with `;` for the three sensor triples, one +{ } per loop body, `@graph obsgraph` in the extracted header) plus `Literal(args[0])`/`Literal(args[1])` written `f{args[0]}`/`f{args[1]}`, the language's coercion of the same values (checked on a str, an int and a float by the driver).
No exception to the symmetry rule: the region was already as compact in Python as the doctrine allows, so the whole gain is the notation's.
